summary: A news-style feature chronicling the fictional rise of blockchain nations from October 2023 to June 2024, framed as a shift comparable to the end of feudalism and the birth of democracy. It follows the Digital Federative Republic, its Block Bit currency, adoption by states like Storvaskia, the Finance Summit, the United Nations of Blockchain, and the first Blockchain Treaty. It also covers resistance from centralized financial institutions and cyber tensions.
one_line: A news feature tracing the 2023-2024 rise of blockchain nations, from the Digital Federative Republic and Block Bit currency to the first Blockchain Treaty.
key_facts: On October 3, 2023, a coalition led by Elaine Muskova and Benjamin D. Thompson declared the Digital Federative Republic (DFR), a sovereign entity built on blockchain technology.
On November 17, 2023, the DFR released its first fiat-alternative digital currency, the Block Bit (BBI), promising autonomy from traditional banks, immediate transactions and lower fees.
DFR citizens came to be known as "Blocktizens".
On January 10, 2024, Storvaskia, led by President Helena Ivić, integrated blockchain technology into its economic reform plans, calling it "The Digital Renaissance".
Countries with economies tied to legacy banking institutions viewed blockchain nations with apprehension and pushed back against decentralization.
The Finance Summit of 2024 on March 3 addressed the ramifications of blockchain nations, focusing on a relationship between existing fiat currencies and the BBI.
Thomas Reed of the American think tank "Prosperity Now" gave a speech on the "Pillars of Trust", calling for a system built on transparency, security and equality.
On April 15, 2024, leaders established the United Nations of Blockchain (UNB) to craft a federated international protocol for transactions, digital rights and virtual asset movement.
"Hash borders" define spheres of cryptographic consensus rather than physical territories.
Digital guilds of programmers, cybersecurity experts and algorithm economists refine smart contracts and decentralized applications.

On June 12, 2024, leaders of the Blockchain Nations and twenty-two traditional countries signed the first Blockchain Treaty, setting standards for digital governance, smart contract diplomacy and decentralized dispute resolution.
New Zealand Prime Minister Aaron Taylor signed the treaty; New Zealand recognized dual digital-and-national citizenship for residents joining the DFR.
Observers dubbed the Blockchain Treaty the "Magna Carta of the Digital Age".
Tensions included cyber skirmishes in which coalitions of hackers squared off instead of armies.
